mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 increases for two consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% MoM signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 2% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000, it signals a strong labor market recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000, and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% YoY signals a strong demand for housing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases > 10% YoY and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative, it signals a recessionary environment with potential for monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 growth < 0%, and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% MoM signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS decreases > 5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
